newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan CATV firm to start cheaper city-call service.
newsitem.headline: Japan CATV firm to start cheaper city-call service.

text.p: Japanese cable television operator (CATV) Titus Communications said on Tuesday that it would start offering city call services in June at rates substantially lower than those offered by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
Titus will start the service in a Tokyo suburb in June, expanding the service to five other cities, including those in Tokyo, next year.
Titus is owned by Itochu Corp, Toshiba Corp, U.S. West International Holding and Time Warner Inc.
The basic monthly rate will be about 25 to 46 percent lower than NTT's rate, Titus said.
The per-minute tariff for the city-call service will be two to four yen, compared with NTT's 10 yen, Titus said.
Titus will offer the service to CATV subscribers as well as others, it said.
